description: In Elixir __MODULE__ in a function body is the enclosing module's atom (Elixir.Foo.Bar), and nil at the top level; %__MODULE__{} is the module's own struct, in a literal and in a pattern. In fz __MODULE__ in a body is 'unresolved value __MODULE__' (unbound variable inside a macro's quote), and %__MODULE__{} is parse/expected-token 'expected uppercase struct path'. The namespace already binds __ENV__ as a Splice symbol just before a body is expanded (src/compiler2/namespace.rs); __MODULE__ is the same mechanism with the module's atom as the spliced value, or a direct lowering through World::module_alias_atom. It must also work in code a macro quotes into the caller's module, where it names the caller's module. Fix in one place, with an oracle fixture on interp, run and build. Needed by defexception (fz-3ul.4). Plan: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-3sy.8.html.
title: __MODULE__ in a function body is the module's atom
